FLEET STATUS UPDATE 2026-08-29 ~19:45 — forge-studio deliberately NOT converged, and it must stay that way until a daemonkit fix lands. Do NOT re-attempt the two-step remedy on it; that is what wedged it.

The unsandboxed `capt-hookd package-install` remedy recorded above CONVERGED yasyf-box but FAILED on yasyf-forge-studio, twice, with a completely different error — never reaching the sandbox issue at all:

    captain package: land delivered app: daemonkit: process did not provably exit
    context deadline exceeded

WHY THE REMEDY DOES NOT GENERALISE, and this is the important part: yasyf-box converged only because its incumbent was 12.21.3, writing to the PRE-v0.22 state root that a v0.23.0 binary cannot see. `hostRecordAbsent()` therefore returned true, `stopInstalledHost()` took the legacy path, and daemonkit's modern drain was never exercised. forge-studio's incumbent was 12.22.3, which HAS a record at the new root, so it went through the modern drain — and the modern drain is broken.

The state-root migration to ~/.daemonkit/a/ means every host is forge-studio's case from now on. The two-step above is a legacy-path accident, not a general remedy, and it stops working the moment a machine's incumbent is on the new root.

WHAT IT COSTS TO TRY ANYWAY: the failed attempt leaves the host alive but socketless, holding its flock with its shutdown abandoned, and the helper down. The app bundle is NOT damaged — inode unchanged, no partial swap — but the daemon is unusable until `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.yasyf.captain-hook.host.v1`, plus `launchctl kickstart gui/$(id -u)/com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper` to bring the helper back. That restored forge-studio cleanly to a healthy 12.22.3 (host pid 30166, helper pid 30172, both status 0, `helper v12.22.3 ok=True`).

The underlying drain defect is daemonkit's and is filed there. Its first domino is a cc-notes hook TypeError (cc-notes bug dee57af) that kills a hook worker whose exit then cannot be proven.

So: yasyf-box is on 12.22.4. yasyf-forge-studio stays on 12.22.3, healthy, one release behind, by decision — converging it would paper over a defect that is now the DEFAULT upgrade path for every host in the fleet.
